question.text: Under the workbook framework, derivatives are classified as securities under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 (SCRA) and derive their value from underlying securities. On this basis, which of the following statements about SEBI's jurisdiction over derivatives trading is correct?

answer.text: Because derivatives are securities under SCRA, SEBI's mandate over securities-market misconduct (such as insider trading and market manipulation in the underlying) extends to trading in derivatives on those securities
Derivatives are not securities under SCRA and SEBI's jurisdiction does not cover them
SEBI's misconduct jurisdiction covers only index derivatives, never single-stock derivatives
Securities-market misconduct rules cease to apply if the trader holds derivatives instead of the underlying shares

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (NISM Series-VIII December 2025, pp.175-176) states that derivatives are securities under SCRA and derive their value from underlying securities. SEBI's mandate over securities-market misconduct - including insider-trading-style allegations referenced on p.214 - therefore extends to derivatives trading on those securities. The keyed option states only this directly source-supported point. The Trap: Saying derivatives are outside SCRA contradicts pp.175-176; restricting jurisdiction to index derivatives or claiming derivatives shield a trader from misconduct rules has no source support. The audit flagged the original because its blanket "PIT 2015 applies equally to derivatives" wording was an inference rather than a direct citation from the workbook. Note: The original was ambiguous because it asserted PIT 2015 coverage of derivatives as an equivalence, which is correct in law but not stated directly in the workbook. The stem and key have been tightened to the narrower SCRA-based point (derivatives are securities, so SEBI's securities-market misconduct mandate covers them), which is the directly source-supported version from NISM Series-VIII December 2025, pp.175-176, p.214.
